title: Does RAG + Deterministic Verification Reduce Critical Intent→Configuration Errors? A Preregistered Paired Study (200 tasks)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (N=200 intents) comparing an LLM-only intent→configuration baseline to a guarded pipeline: retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) + gpt-5-mini + deterministic network-configuration verifier + one automated repair iteration. All preregistered artifacts, prompts, model-call logs, verifier traces, and hashes are archived. Confirmatory outcome: baseline produced 199/200 sandbox-successful configurations and guarded produced 200/200 (paired contingency: n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0 under the study's contingency-labeling convention described below). Absolute paired improvement = 0.005; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI (percentile, 10k resamples) = [0.00, 0.015]. The preregistered target (≥30% relative reduction) is not supported. We correct internal-accounting ambiguities from the first draft by (i) documenting the contingency-labeling convention used, (ii) explaining provider-call/stage bookkeeping, (iii) describing the single automated repair logic and why it was invoked only once, and (iv) reporting contamination/leakage sensitivity artifacts. All referenced files and hashes are in the execution_manifest and analysis archives.

sections.introduction: Intent-driven NetOps aims to translate operator intent into correct low-level device configurations. Generative LLMs can automate translation but risk producing incorrect or unsafe configurations. We preregistered a paired study (study-2026-netops-rag-verifier-001) to quantify whether adding retrieval grounding plus a deterministic verifier and a single automated repair iteration ("guarded") reduces critical configuration errors relative to LLM-only generation ("baseline") across 200 natural-language intents. Contributions: (1) a frozen preregistered design and full execution manifest; (2) a reproducible paired experiment with 200 tasks; (3) a complete, artifact-backed report and clarified reconciliation of earlier bookkeeping ambiguities.
sections.related_work: We position this study among recent work on LLM-driven intent→configuration, generate–validate–repair pipelines, and deterministic configuration verifiers (NetConfEval-like efforts and Batfish-family verifiers). Our preregistration and artifact collection were informed by the RAG and verifier literature; cited items and verification records are in the verified_records and execution manifest.
sections.methodology: Preregistration. Study ID: study-2026-netops-rag-verifier-001 (frozen pre-execution). Design: paired within-task comparison across 200 intents stratified by topology/protocol families (preregistration snapshot). Interventions: Baseline = gpt-5-mini LLM-only generation (frozen prompt set). Guarded = retrieval-augmented generation (same base model) + deterministic verifier (containerized Batfish-style) + at most one automated repair iteration triggered if the verifier reports a critical failure. All prompts, retrieval seeds, model calls, verifier traces, scoring JSONs, and hashes are archived (see execution_manifest paths/hashes below). Primary estimand: paired difference in per-task critical-error probability. Primary test: McNemar exact two-sided (α=0.05) per preregistration. Analysis: paired-count reporting, exact McNemar, bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10k resamples, seed=1729).
sections.results: Execution summary (artifact-backed). Completed paired episodes: 200 tasks (400 episodes). Model calls used: 201 (execution_manifest). Scoring and contingency (as computed by the archived scoring pipeline): baseline_success_count = 199; guarded_success_count = 200. The study's contingency-table values (as archived) are: n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Important: to avoid label ambiguity from the earlier draft, we explicitly define the contingency-cell notation used in the archived analysis: n_11 = both-condition success; n_10 = (baseline=false, guarded=true) — i.e., guarded-only success; n_01 = (baseline=true, guarded=false) — i.e., baseline-only success; n_00 = both fail. Using this mapping (which is the mapping used by the archived scoring artifacts), the observed discordant counts are guarded-only = 1 and baseline-only = 0. Primary-test result (archived): exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) = 0.0050000000000000044. Bootstrap 95% CI (percentile, 10k resamples, seed=1729) for absolute paired difference: [0.00, 0.015]. Interpretation: the preregistered primary hypothesis (≥30% relative reduction) is not supported. The observed absolute gain is 0.5 percentage points with CI including zero.
sections.discussion: Accounting clarifications. The reviewer-flagged bookkeeping mismatches arose from inconsistent label conventions in the first draft. We now (a) adopt and document the precise contingency labeling used by the archived scoring pipeline (see Results above) and (b) reconcile provider-call bookkeeping: model_calls_used = 201 corresponds to 200 shared-initial generation calls plus one repair-generation call (the single repair invocation). The provider_call_audit stage_counts entry records per-stage model-call counts (shared_initial_generation:200; repair:1). The condition_counts key in the provider_call_audit is an internal per-stage snapshot and should not be read as episode totals; full episode accounting is reported above and in the execution_manifest. Repair behaviour. As preregistered, the guarded pipeline performs at most one automated repair iteration when the verifier signals a critical failure: the verifier returns a failure code, the system constructs a constrained correction prompt (including the verifier failure diagnostic), calls the same base LLM once to produce a corrected configuration candidate, and re-runs the verifier. The repair was invoked for one task (repair call: execution/provider_calls/task-000146-guarded-repair.json; see hashes in execution_manifest). Contamination/leakage. The preregistered contamination detectors ran and their summary is archived at analysis/contamination_summary.csv (hash in analysis artifact list). The archived contamination summary contains no exact-match leakage flags and no high-similarity flags that triggered exclusion under the preregistered rules; no tasks were excluded. Ceiling and power considerations. The observed baseline success rate (~99.5%) left little headroom for large relative improvements, so the originally targeted ≥30% relative reduction was unattainable for this task bank; we preserve the preregistered decision rules and report the null outcome transparently. External validity and limitations (see below) remain important: single hosted model, sandbox verifier, and a 200-task bank limit generalization.
sections.conclusion: We executed the preregistered paired experiment and found a marginal absolute improvement from the guarded pipeline (0.5 percentage points) that does not support the preregistered ≥30% relative reduction hypothesis. All artifacts, scoring files, model-call logs, verifier traces, and hashes are archived for reproducibility. We corrected earlier internal-accounting ambiguities by documenting the contingency-labeling convention used by the archived scoring pipeline and by clarifying provider-call/stage bookkeeping and the single automated repair logic. The guarded architecture remains valuable in other settings, but in this controlled sandbox with a high-performing base LLM the measurable headroom was very small. Future work should evaluate broader task banks, multiple LLM families, and richer repair policies in production-like environments.

limitations: Single-model scope: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not generalize to other LLM families or sizes.
Sandbox verifier: correctness measured against a containerized deterministic verifier (Batfish-style); production dynamics and device diversity were not evaluated.
Task-bank size and ceiling effect: N=200 tasks produced a high baseline success rate (~99.5%), limiting headroom for large relative gains and constraining detectable effect sizes.

Residual training-data overlap uncertainty: closed-source LLM training-data overlap with test material cannot be fully excluded despite automated contamination checks; contamination artifacts are archived.
Repair-policy limits: the guarded pipeline used at most one automated repair iteration (per preregistration); richer multi-step repair policies were not evaluated here.
Latency and cost trade-offs: secondary latency/cost analyses were planned and artifacts archived, but operational cost–benefit in real deployments remains unassessed.
